question.text: In a quadrilateral $ABCD,$ the measures of the sides are ${AB} = 17\,\mathrm{mm},$ ${BC} = 14\,\mathrm{mm},$ ${CD} = 2\,\mathrm{cm},$ and ${DA} = 9\,\mathrm{mm}.$ What is the perimeter of the quadrilateral?
question.explanation:
Most of the measures are given in $\mathrm{mm}$ (millimeters), so we will start by converting all the measures to $\mathrm{mm}$ and adding them up: \begin{align*} p &= 17\,\mathrm{mm} + 14\,\mathrm{mm} + \overbrace{20\,\mathrm{mm}}^{\large 2\,\mathrm{cm}} + 9\,\mathrm{mm} \\[2pt] &= 60\,\mathrm{mm} \end{align*}

Finally, since the perimeter is a large quantity of $\textrm{mm},$ we will convert to $\textrm{cm}\mathbin{:}$

\[ p = 60\, \mathrm{mm} = 6\,\mathrm{cm}. \]

example.title: Calculating the Perimeter of a Polygon

question.text: In the regular octagon $ABCDEFGH$, we have $CD=1.5\, \mathrm{cm}.$ What is the perimeter of the octagon?
question.explanation: The perimeter $p$ of a polygon is the sum of the measures of all its sides. Since all the sides of a regular octagon are equal and the measure of one of them is $1.5\, \mathrm{cm}$, we have \[ p = 8\cdot CD = 8\cdot 1.5 = 12\, \mathrm{cm}. \]
